newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Wednesday on short-selling by retail investors, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,328 yuan ($401) per tonne, up six yuan. It opened at 3,348 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,350 and a low of 3,327.
January fell six to 3,238 yuan per tonne, March four to 3,233, May did not trade, July fell 19 to 3,360 and September was unchanged at 3,380.
Combined volume fell to 6,400 tonnes from 6,500.
Traders said most investors stayed on the sidelines due to the dull market mood.
"Short-selling by retail investors dominated today's trading but the market trend was still unclear due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders expect soybean to be stable over the next few days.
